sentences.text: This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 30-09-2016 at around 8-00 p.m., the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 04-EM-6251 from Bhuhalli village towards Harihara village along with pillion rider by name Mahadeva.

When they reached near Kurabanakatte village, near Bhuhalli, Sathanoor Hobli, at that time, a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-W-0581 belonging to the 1st respondent came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Kanakapura Government Hospital and then shifted to Rajarajeshwari Hospital,
Bangalore, wherein admitted as an inpatient.
So far the petitioner has spent Rs.63,000/- towards medical, conveyance and other expenses.

Prior to the accident,
the petitioner was hale and healthy.
The petitioner was doing agricultural and coolie and thereby earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Due to permanent disability petitioner is not in a position to do the said work.
He has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of income, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
3. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1/ R.C. owner of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-W-0581 remained absent.
Hence he was placed ex-parte.

4. Respondent No.2-National Insurance Co.Ltd.,/ Limited/insurer of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42- W-0581 has filed the written statement and contended that there is delay of 13 days in lodging the complaint, that as per police records it was mentioned that, unknown Hero Honda Splender caused the accident, hence the offending vehicle is not at all involved in the alleged accident.
It is further contended that the rider of offending motorcycle was not holding valid driving licence and the said vehicle was not having permit as on the date of accident.
It is further contended that the petitioner was riding motorcycle without having driving licence and without having valid policy.
5. On the basis of the above pleadings following Issues were framed.

: I S S U E S:
1.

Whether petitioner proves that on 30.09.2016 at about 8.00 p.m. he was riding his Motor cycle bearing No.KA-04-EM-6251 towards Bhuhalli village to Harihara village along with another person when they reached near Kurabanakatte village, Near Bhuhalli, Sathanoor Hobli at that time the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42- Siddaraju H.S vs Siddaramu on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60105360/
2 W-0581 belonging to 1st respondent rode it in high speed, rash and negligent manner endangering to human life and caused the accident because of which he sustained grievous injuries and he became permanently disabled as contended in the petition ?
2. Whether respondent No.2 proves that the accident in question took place solely due to carelessness and negligence of petitioner?
3. Whether respondent No.2 proves that delay in lodging the FIR would exempt him from liability?

4. Whether respondent No.2 proves that as on the date of accident rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-42-W-0581 and rider/petitioner of motor cycle bearing No.KA-04-EM-6251 are not possessed valid and effective driving licenses to drive the motor cycles respectively?
5. Whether respondent No.2 proves that the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-42- W-0581 is falsely implicated in the accident?
6. Whether respondent No.2 proves that jurisdictional police have violated the mandatory provision of Section 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act ?
7. Whether respondent No.2 proves that the respondent No. has violated the mandatory provision of Section 134(C) of Motor Vehicles Act?
8. Whether the petitioner proves he is entitled for compensation as sought for?
9. What Order or Award?
6.
In order to prove the case, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to 13.
On the hand, the respondent no.1 has examined Sri.Chandrashekaraish.D -Office Superintendent, Ramanagara RTO, Channapattana as RW.1 and got marked documents as Ex.R1 to 8.
K.M Sundar Raju - the Retired PSI at Kanakapura is examined as Rw.2.

Bhaskar C- Police Inspector is examined as RW.3 and the respondent no.1 has examined its Assistant Manager as RW.4 and got marked documents as Ex.R9 to Ex.R15.
7.
Heard arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner and respondent no.1 and perused the entire materials placed on record.

8. My findings on the above-referred Issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 :-In the Negative  Issue No.2, 3 &5 :- In the affirmative  Issue No.4, 6 & 7 : Does not survive for  Consideration  Issue No.8 : In the Negative  Issue No.9 : As per the final order,
 for the following.

3  :REASONS:
 9. Issue No.1 to 7 : - As these issues are interconnected they are taken up together for common discussion to avoid repetition of facts.
10.

In order to explain the actionable negligence of the rider of offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 30-09-2016 at around 8-00 p.m. when petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 04-EM-6251 from Bhuhalli village towards Harihara village along with pillion rider by name Mahadeva and when they reached near Kurabanakatte village, near Bhuhalli, Sathanoor Hobli, at that time, a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-W-0581 belonging to the 1st respondent came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries 11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 6 which are the police records such as F.I.R., Complaint, spot mahazar, seizer mahazar, wound certificate, charge sheet, etc.
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Roopa, case has been registered against the rider of offending vehicle in Crime No.0184/2016 of Sathnoor Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 338 of IPC and Sec.187 of IMV Act.

After completion of investigation, the investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under section 279, 338 of IPC and u/Sec. 187 of IMV Act.

13. The learned counsel for respondent no.2 has seriously disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident and submitted that the rider and owner of the offending vehicle being the close relatives of the petitioner and hails from same village colluding with each other has filed false complaint against the accused by falsely implicating the offending vehicle in the accident.

It is vehemently argued by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 that the petitioner, respondent no.1,
accused and police officials of jurisdictional police colluding together have played fraud upon the court as well as upon insurance company in order to gain unlawful enrichment at the cost of respondent no.2, hence submit to dismiss the claim petition.

The learned counsel for respondent no.2 at this juncture has referred the judgment reported in AIR 2000 SC 1165 between United India Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Rajendra Singh & Ors., and ILR 2009 KAR 3562 rendered by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, (Circuit Bench at Gulbarga between Veerappa & Anr., Vs. Siddappa & Anr., and ILR 2009 Kar 2921 between Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co.Ltd.. Vs. B.C Kumar & Anr.

sentences.text: The said rulings has been referred by the learned counsel with reference to the observation made by the Hon'ble High Court and Supreme Court in the case of fraud played by the petitioner in claiming the compensation.

14. In the light of the observation made in the aforesaid judgment so also in the light of the line of argument canvassed by the learned counsel for the respondent no.2, if the materials placed on record are carefully perused, it is not in dispute that the alleged accident has occurred on 30-09-2016 at about 8-00 p.m.

As per the case of petitioner he was the rider of motorcycle bearing Siddaraju H.S vs Siddaramu on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60105360/
4 No.KA-04-EM-6251.
From the materials placed on record it can further be gathered that the complaint was lodged by the wife of petitioner on 12-10-2015 i.e., after lapse of nearly 13 days from the date of accident.

In the complaint and in the FIR reason for delay has been explained stating that the family members of the accused requested the petitioner not to lodge the complaint and they will bear the medical expenses, but they have failed to keep up their promise.
Further because of lack of knowledge and as complainant had small kids she could not lodge the complaint in time.
15. If the cross examination of PW.1 is perused, as admitted by him, after the accident he was in conscious state of mind.
From the evidence of PW.1 it can be gathered that the rider and owner of the alleged offending vehicle are the relatives of the petitioner and all the three are from same village.

In the complaint which was given on 12-10-2016, the registration number of the alleged offending vehicle is not mentioned but only mentioned that unregistered Hero Honda Splendor ridden by Santhosh hit against the motorcycle of the petitioner and caused the accident.
From the evidence of RW.1 who is the office Superintendent, Ramanagar RTO it can be gathered that at the time of alleged accident, the alleged offending vehicle had no registration number.

Temporary registration number as per Ex.P6 was given from their RTO and the temporary registration certificate was in force till 14-09-2016 and on 05-10-2016 permanent registration certificate was given.
It means as on the date of accident, the alleged offending vehicle had no permanent registration number.
It is on 05-10-2016 permanent registration number was given.

When admittedly respondent no.1 is the relative of the petitioner and they are from the same village and when complaint was lodged on 12-10-2016, under such circumstances in the delayed complaint lodged by the wife of petitioner they could have mentioned the registration number of the vehicle involved in the accident, but vehicle number is not mentioned in the complaint.
16. It is further relevant to state here that on the date of lodging the complaint itself i.e., on 12-10-2016 spot mahazar as per Ex.P3 was drawn.
But for the reason best known to the petitioner they have not produced the sketch of the scene of occurrence.

Though in the complaint it is stated that unregistered motorcycle ridden by Santhosh hit against the motorcycle of petitioner and though Santhosh and owner of the said vehicle are from the place of petitioner but very strangely the alleged offending vehicle was seized on 21-02-2017 under Ex.P4 seizer mahazar.

As per the evidence of Rw.3 i.e the investigating officer, during the course of investigation they have deputed PS 62 to trace the alleged offending vehicle and after tracing the said vehicle, the said vehicle was seized under the mahazar.

At the cost of repetition when the owner and rider of the alleged offending vehicle are the relatives of the petitioner and when they are from the same village and when in the complaint the name of the rider of alleged offending vehicle is mentioned under such circumstances the question of tracing the said vehicle through the police officials does not arise because in the complaint itself they have stated the unregistered vehicle ridden by Santhosh hit against the vehicle of the petitioner.
Further as per the evidence of RW.3 the accused has surrendered before the I.O on 21-02-2017.

As observed supra, when in the complaint the complainant has stated that the unregistered Hero Honda motorcycle ridden by Santhosh of their village hit against the vehicle of the petitioner , under such circumstances on the date of registering the FIR itself the investigating officer could have taken steps to arrest the accused.
Hence, the reason for delay of nearly 130 days in seizer of alleged offending vehicle and arresting the accused is not forthcoming in the charge sheet.

As rightly argued by the learned counsel for respondent no.2, in the complaint nowhere the registration number of the Siddaraju H.S vs Siddaramu on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60105360/
5
alleged
offending vehicle is mentioned.
Further the re -statement of complainant, petitioner and alleged eye witness by name Mahadeva was recorded on 25-02-2017.
In the re statement of the aforesaid witnesses, for the first time they have mentioned the registration number of the alleged offending vehicle.

But it is prior to the said witnesses disclosed the registration number of the alleged offending vehicle in their re- statement, the said vehicle was seized under Ex.P4.
17.

As per the case of petitioner, soon after the accident he got admitted at Government Hospital,
Kanakapura and thereafter he got admitted at Rajarajeshwari Hospital, Bangalore.

Though petitioner has submitted that he has no objection to produce the MLC register of Kanakapura Government Hospital and Rajarajeshwari Hospital but for the reason best known to him he has not produced the said material documents.
He even has not produced the police intimation.

Though PW.2 who is the treated doctor at Rajarajeshwari Hospital has deposed that they have sent police intimation but RW.3 who is an investigating officer has deposed that no police intimation is sent from the Hospital.
When there is serious dispute raised regarding the involvement of alleged offending vehicle, the petitioner could have produced the MLC register and police intimation.
But as observed supra for the reason best known to the petitioner he has not produced the said documents.
Further in the discharge summary issued from Rajarajeshwari Hospital at Ex.P8 the history of injury is mentioned as "RTA" but nowhere, the involvement of another two wheeler is mentioned.

When petitioner was conscious at the time of his admission to the hospital and when accused is known to the petitioner, if really the alleged offending vehicle was involved in the accident, nothing prevented the petitioner from giving information to the hospital authority about involvement of vehicle of Santhosh in the accident.
18.
The learned counsel for respondent no.2 has produced the records pertaining to criminal case registered against the driver of alleged offending vehicle by name Santhosh.
In the said case, after the arrest of accused by name Santhosh he was released on police bail by executing indemnity bond at Ex.R12 wherein the said Santhosh has signed in English as" Santhosh A S.'
As per the charge sheet the name of accused is Santhosh but not Santhosh A S.
Further in the plea of the accused recorded in CC No.844/2017 marked as Ex.R14 the accused has signed in Kannada as "".

Hence the person alleged to be the driver of alleged offending vehicle appeared before the police station to execute the bond and the person who appeared before the JMFC Court as accused appears to be different persons.
If they are the same person then he would have signed the bail bond and plea form in same form but not in different form.

19. It is further relevant to state here that though the respondent no.2 has seriously disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident but the petitioner has not taken any steps to examine any independent witness to prove the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.

As per the case of petitioner, one Mahadeva was the pillion rider in the two wheeler ridden by him and even in the alleged offending vehicle pillion rider was there and they are the eye witness to the accident.
But very strangely the petitioner has not examined even Mahadeva as witness in the present case.
Nothing prevented the petitioner from examining Mahadeva as witness to prove his case.

sentences.text: Hence, the materials placed on record clearly proves that the offending vehicle is not at all involved in the accident.

In order to claim compensation, the petitioner in collusion with the police officials, driver and owner of the alleged offending vehicle has falsely implicated the offending vehicle in the accident, hence only there is delay in lodging the complaint so also there is delay in arresting the alleged accused and seizer of alleged offending vehicle.

When the alleged offending vehicle is not at all involved in the accident, the question the driver of the alleged offending vehicle driving the said vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and causing the accident would not arise.

Hence, issue no.1 is answered in the Negative and issue no.2 in the affirmative, issue no.3 in the affirmative, issue no.5 in the affirmative and issue no.4, 6 and 7 does not arise for consideration.
21. Issue no 8 : When petitioner has failed to prove that the accident in question has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the alleged offending vehicle as the involvement of alleged offending vehicle in the accident itself is doubtful, under such circumstances the petitioner is not entitled for compensation.
Hence, issue no.8 is answered in the Negative.
22. Issue No.9:
In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 to 7, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby dismissed.
Draw award accordingly.
